title: node.set_route, contract version 2
description: Sets a node's route on a site in one language (PRD 5.9) in one changeset: the route is the path the public asks for, and the longest route that is a prefix of a request's path decides the node, while the rest of the path is the slug of a placement below it. The document is version 1's; version 2 differs in what it does with a node that has a route on the site in that language already: it moves the route and records the one the node had as a prefix redirect, so every URL below the old route answers 301 below the new one in one hop, also after several changes, while version 1 refuses such a node. A node without a route gets one, as version 1 gives it. A route that moves makes nothing public that was not, so an agent may move one; the first route of a node makes it reachable from the public internet, and an agent or a token is refused with agent_visibility_forbidden. The issuing actor needs node.set_route on the node in the language, and a node its grants do not reach is unauthorized. A node at another version than the caller read, and a route another command claimed between the read and the commit, are version_conflict; a route another node holds already is node_route_taken. A node that is archived, a site the installation does not have, a language the site does not publish in, a node that is not below the site's root, and the route the node has already are validation_failed. The PHP form is Cbox\Cms\Core\Structure\Domain\Commands\ChangeNodeRoute, and the generated codec ChangeNodeRouteCodecV2 reads it and writes its canonical JSON: every key, sorted, no whitespace.

node.description: The id of the node to address.

version.description: The version of the node the caller read.

site.description: The id of the site the route is on.

locale.description: The language the route is in, one the site publishes in.

route.description: The route the node gets: / or segments of no slash and no white space, at most 32 segments and 2048 bytes, without . or .. segments and without a trailing slash. The route the node had, if any, becomes a prefix redirect to it.

locale.description: A language tag of a language, an optional script and an optional region, such as da, en-GB or sr-Latn-RS; the kernel writes the language in lowercase, the script in title case and the region in uppercase.

version.description: The version of an aggregate that the caller read, an integer of 1 or more; the command is version_conflict when the aggregate is at another version when it commits.
